svg.aria-label: Diagram: the three Policy Intelligence tools that answer who has access, why access was denied and what a change would break, the different part of the access decision each one omits, the Policy Simulator hard limits on log replay and conditions, and the fact that all three report what they could not evaluate
svg.title: Policy Intelligence: three tools, three different omissions, all of them stated on the page
svg.text: Three tools that answer who, why and what-if — each omitting a different part.
And the omissions are precisely the access-control mechanisms the previous twenty-seven posts covered.
Three questions, three tools
Question
Tool
What it reads
Who can do what here?
Policy Analyzer
the allow policy, via Cloud Asset API
Why was this request denied?
Policy Troubleshooter
the policies bearing on one request
What breaks if I change it?
Policy Simulator
90 days of access logs, replayed
Each one omits a different part of the access decision
Analyzer: ONLY IAM allow policies. Not deny. Not PAB. Not GKE RBAC. Not Cloud Storage ACLs or PAP.
Troubleshooter: no Cloud Storage ACLs, and it does not diagnose VPC Service Controls at all.
Troubleshooter: does not fetch tags for REGIONAL resources, so tag-based conditions may be wrong.
Simulator: only evaluates allow policies, and does not support conditions at all.
And the Simulator has a hard stop, not a degradation
It replays at most 5,000 access logs. Above that, for 90 days of a project or org, the
simulation FAILS, so the biggest estates are the ones that cannot simulate.
A conditional binding comes back Unsupported condition: it could not be evaluated.
And it needs permission to read group membership, or the result is Membership info denied.
What they get right, and it is the important part
All three report what they could NOT evaluate: unsupported permissions are listed, conditions
are marked CONDITIONAL, unknown results carry a reason, and errors are surfaced to review.
These are instruments with stated error bars. The failure mode is reading the answer and
skipping the caveat, which is the same failure as every other post in this block.
Freshness is best-effort: almost all policy updates appear in minutes, but not guaranteed.
Expansion caps: 1,000 per group, 1,000 per resource, 100,000 for a longrunning query.
#57 measured usage through one system. #58 answers who-can-do-what through one system too,
and names the other five on the page. The tools are honest; a single-pane answer is not.
